title: Table S4. FTA ranking comparison and scale-up decision
note: Population: 87 adjudicated-analysable RSv1 records, Main 11-50 within each pair. Improvement-related targets occurred in 49 records, comprising 62 report-category occurrences; recall@5 was 7/62. Targets combined adjudicated HFACS leaf categories with verbatim improvement quotations and reviewer-added categories, deduplicated within each report. Frequency counts reports containing a leaf category; co-occurrence counts weighted within-report category co-occurrences. FTA ranks categories by interruption of the generated AND/OR tree when their leaves are set false, with minimal-cut-set coverage as a tie-breaker. NDCG is normalised discounted cumulative gain.
paragraphs: Scale-up conditions: recall-difference lower 95% confidence bound > 0, not met; minimum FTA top-five selection rate >= 0.70, met (0.861); top five different from frequency, not met; no improvement-quotation leakage flags, met. Overall decision: do not scale up.

Observed FTA-minus-frequency recall@5 difference: 0.000. The 2,000-resample percentile interval was -0.415 to 0.194, with rankings recomputed in each resample. The saved bootstrap mean (-0.084) is not the observed difference.

title: Table S5. FTA versus direct classification: primary RSv1 comparison
note: Both methods used Kimi K2.5 and event description plus background, without improvement measures. The reference was the report-level set of retained adjudicated RSv1 HFACS leaf categories plus reviewer-added categories. Mean precision and recall were calculated per report and then averaged. Micro metrics pooled report-category true positives, false positives, and false negatives; repeated categories within a report counted once. Paired differences use the same records, with 95% percentile intervals from 2,000 record-cluster bootstrap resamples. L3/L4 metrics pooled the categories in those two layers.

title: Table S6. Sensitivity and alternative-target analyses of FTA versus direct classification
note: Main 1-50 includes all 112 adjudicated-analysable RSv1 records. The traceable-quotation analysis retained predictions linked to quotations locatable in event description or background; this is a traceability filter, not a full-support judgement. The alternative improvement-related target analysis used the 49 records with nonempty targets defined in Table S4. Means assigned precision 1 when both prediction and reference were empty, precision 0 when only the prediction was empty, and recall 1 when the reference was empty. Differences and 95% percentile intervals use 2,000 paired record-cluster resamples. These analyses reuse RSv1 records with alternative populations or prediction/reference conditions.
